card.title: IPad Pro 12.9 5th Gen not powering on due to long screw damage

source.title: IPad Pro 12.9 5th Gen not powering on due to long screw damage

claims.statement: On iPad Pro 12.9 (5th/6th gen) putting the long shield screw in the wrong standoff by the battery connector can break the PP3V3_BSB line or its via, leaving the iPad dead after a screen repair.
Symptoms: 0 A before power-on and only 0.014–0.025 A after on a DC supply; USB meter shows ~0.02 A, a jump to ~0.5 A, then near zero; pressing near the standoff may let it boot.
Fix: remove the standoff, scrape to the via, and jumper from the line at C8300 to the via; clamping the standoff can allow a one-time data backup.

procedure: Look for long-screw damage at the standoff above the screen FPCs.
Remove the standoff; scrape carefully around it.
Check the PP3V3_BSB via/line from C8300.
Jumper C8300 line to the via; verify boot; conformal coat.
cautions: SOURCE RISK: The longer shield screw in the wrong standoff causes this damage.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
